headline: Alice and friends come to Oyster Bay

headline: Drives and tennis with his 'Queen'
summary: Roosevelt revels in having Alice at Oyster Bay. He takes her on a carriage ride to Laurelton and Syosset with Rose and Ike Iselin riding behind, plays tennis after lunch, and passes the evening alone with her in the garden summer house.

events.detail: Carriage ride to Laurelton and Syosset with Alice, Rose and Ike Iselin
Afternoon tennis
Evening with Alice in the summer house

tr_quotes.text: It is perfectly delightful to have my sweet Queen here.

headline: A full house at Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt takes Alice on a morning drive through the Long Island countryside, goes sailing with the group after lunch, and visits Uncle Jim's in the evening. Houseguests Douglas Robinson and Romy Colgate swell the party at home.

Afternoon sail with the party
Evening visit to Uncle Jim's and the cousins

headline: A Fourth of July vow of love
summary: After church, Roosevelt walks Alice through Fleets woods and down to the dock in the evening. In his diary he pours out his devotion, writing that no hardship could shake her loyalty and that his love will only deepen with time.

events.detail: Attends church in the morning
Long walk with Alice through Fleets woods
Evening stroll down to the dock
Records his feelings for Alice in his diary

tr_quotes.text: How I love her! and I would trust her to the end of the world.
No matter how long I live I know my love for her will only grow deeper and tenderer day by day; and she shall always be mistress over all that I have.

headline: Pond lilies and a condolence letter

events.detail: Morning drive with Alice
Evening tea at Aunt Annie's

tr_quotes.text: How intensely happy I am: Most of the day is spent with my love.

Tea at the Beekmans'

Evening with Alice in the summer house

summary: Roosevelt says his days with Alice feel like a dream of happiness.

events.detail: Day with Alice

tr_quotes.text: I am living in a dream of delight with my darling, my true-love.

headline: Last parting before the wedding
summary: Roosevelt reluctantly returns to New York in the evening, comforted that this is the final separation: the wedding is just over three weeks away.

events.detail: Returns to New York in the evening

tr_quotes.text: it makes me so happy I am almost afraid.

headline: Wedding errands and law school
summary: Staying with Aunt Annie and Uncle Jimmie Gracie in their snug New York house, Roosevelt busies himself with wedding gifts and preparations. He also enrolls at Columbia Law School.

headline: First day at Columbia Law
summary: Roosevelt begins classes at Columbia Law School, where he will spend about six hours a day. He plans Alice's gifts, a diamond crescent, ruby bracelet and sapphire ring worth about $2,500, and vows to be thriftier once married. His wedding gifts alone ultimately cost $3,889.

events.detail: Starts attending Columbia Law School
Chooses jewelry gifts for Alice

tr_quotes.text: Three weeks from today we are married! I hardly dare believe it; it is too good.

headline: Dinner at Edith Carow's
summary: Two weeks before the wedding, Roosevelt dines at the home of his childhood friend Edith Carow, joined by Fanny Smith and Grace Potter, all of whom will attend. Fanny finds him wild with excitement.

headline: Last bachelor Sunday at Oyster Bay
summary: Knowing his next visit to Oyster Bay will be with his bride, Roosevelt prays he can make Alice happy and resolves to be as unselfish and cheerful as she is.

events.detail: Reflects on marriage and his hopes for Alice's happiness

headline: Naming the wedding party
summary: Roosevelt heads into New York to wrap up business before leaving for Boston on Friday. He records the wedding party: Corinne, Rosy Lee, Rose Saltonstall and Fanny Peabody as bridesmaids, and ten ushers including cousins Emlen and West Roosevelt.

headline: To Chestnut Hill, then Kernwood
summary: Roosevelt hurries out to Chestnut Hill in the morning to embrace Alice, who has received some 250 wedding presents. In the afternoon he goes with his friend Cottie Peabody to the Peabody estate, Kernwood, in Salem, and admires both the place and the bright, well-read family.

events.detail: Joins Alice at Chestnut Hill
Goes with Cottie Peabody to Kernwood
Guest of the Peabody family

headline: Church in Salem and tea with Fanny Peabody
summary: Roosevelt and Cottie walk into Salem for church, then he calls on old 'Grandma Lee.' They take tea at Fanny Peabody's, and he meets Frank Peabody's fiancée, Rosamund Laurence, whom he finds handsome and cultivated.

events.detail: Walks to church in Salem with Cottie
Visits Grandma Lee
Tea at Fanny Peabody's
Meets Rosamund Laurence, engaged to Frank

uncertain: 'Frank' read as Frank Peabody, since the fiancée is staying at the Peabodys'.

headline: Final arrangements, and some tree-felling
summary: Roosevelt settles the last wedding details and in the evening cuts down trees and fools around with Cottie Peabody. Elliott checks in at Boston's Brunswick Hotel, bringing Fanny Smith, Grace Potter and Edith Carow.

events.detail: Finalizes wedding plans
Chops trees with Cottie Peabody
Elliott and three young women friends check into a Boston hotel

headline: Eve of the wedding
summary: Roosevelt comes into Boston, lunches with both families at the Lees', and dines and sleeps at the Brunswick. Elliott will be his best man. At dinner he tips Fanny Smith's chair so far back she fears a backward somersault.

events.detail: Goes from Salem into Boston

headline: Roosevelt marries Alice Lee
summary: On his 22nd birthday, Roosevelt marries Alice Hathaway Lee at noon in Brookline's Unitarian church, with Elliott as best man. After a reception at the Lee home, where Edith Carow dances the evening away, the couple leave around 4 p.m. for a suite in Springfield.

events.detail: Roosevelt's 22nd birthday

Reception at the Lee home
Newlyweds leave about 4 p.m. for Springfield

tr_quotes.text: At 12 o'clock, on my 22d birthday, Alice and I were married.
Our intense happiness is too sacred to be written about.

headline: Honeymoon begins at Oyster Bay
summary: The newlyweds travel from Springfield through New York to Oyster Bay for a two-week stay, with the house to themselves apart from two servants and a groom.

events.detail: Travels with Alice from Springfield via New York to Oyster Bay

headline: Alice rests
summary: Alice spends the day recovering from the trip.

headline: Honeymoon routine
summary: Roosevelt's horse is in fine shape for lovely drives, the tennis court is marked out and his rowboat is afloat. The couple breakfast at ten, dine at two and take tea at seven.

events.detail: Drives with Alice
Settles into a daily routine with Alice

tr_quotes.text: We breakfast at 10; dine at 2; and take tea at 7.

headline: Bible, autumn walks and Dickens
summary: Instead of church, Roosevelt reads the Bible aloud, and the couple walk among hills turned red and gold. While Alice sews he reads to her from Quentin Durward, The Pickwick Papers and The Newcomes. He writes his mother that the honeymoon at Tranquility is a joy.
